study_label: Auditory peripersonal space in humans. (a)
title: Auditory peripersonal space in humans.
experiment_label: Experiment 1 — right-side front/back × near/far × sound type
auditory_stimulus: Static free-field wideband white-noise bursts and 1.5-kHz pure tones, level-adjusted to 70 dB at the ear and emitted by a 0.3-W, 8-ohm loudspeaker under sensor/switch control; reusable source waveforms are not supplied.
trajectory_kinematics: Static right-front and right-back sources at 20 or 70 cm from the head, ear level and 45 degrees from the sagittal plane; sound lasts for the tactile contact (brief, under 1 s), so motion speed is not applicable.
trial_sequence: One tactile-only baseline condition plus eight cross-modal blocks (2 sound types x front/back x 20/70 cm). Each 40-trial block used 10 single-left, 10 single-right, 10 bilateral/simultaneous and 10 no-stimulation rows in the same pseudorandom order; the full protocol ran twice.
task_response: After an experimenter attention prompt, participants verbally reported left, right, both, or none after each event, regardless of modality.
jitter_iti_policy: No ITI, inter-trial interval, jitter value, or distribution was recovered after the main-PDF, targeted, fallback, and supplement-route checks.
soa_schedule: Cross-modal sound and touch were simultaneous (nominal 0-ms SOA); there was no varied SOA ladder.
tactile_target: Brief light contact under 1 s with a 1-cm² touch-sensitive sensor on the lateral neck behind the ear, below the mastoid process.
baseline_trial_contract: Tactile-only switch-off baseline with the same manual contact timing: one 40-trial condition x two protocol runs = 80 baseline-block trials (60 tactile-present and 20 no-stimulation).
catch_trial_contract: No-stimulation rows required a 'none' report: 9 conditions x 10 no-stimulation trials x 2 protocol runs = 180, of which 160 were in cross-modal blocks and 20 in tactile-only baseline blocks.
repetition_allocation: Nine condition blocks, each with 10 repetitions of four trial types, repeated in two complete protocol runs: 9 x 40 x 2 = 720 trials per participant (640 cross-modal-block trials and 80 baseline-block trials).
block_order_contract: Nine condition-specific 40-trial blocks per protocol, with condition-block order randomized across sessions and participants; the complete protocol was repeated twice, yielding 18 blocks.

trial_sequence: Two cross-modal white-noise condition blocks (left-back 20 and 70 cm), each retaining the 40-trial, four-row structure and pseudorandom trial order used in Experiment 1.

study_label: Dynamic sounds capture the boundaries of peripersonal space representation in humans. (a)
title: Dynamic sounds capture the boundaries of peripersonal space representation in humans.
auditory_stimulus: A 44.1-kHz pink-noise sample was shaped in SoundForge 4.5 into 3-s IN (55-to-70 dB) and OUT (70-to-55 dB) envelopes, with identical copies crossfaded simultaneously between near and far physical speakers; the exact noise asset and edit project are unavailable.
trajectory_kinematics: Apparent motion along the right-hand near/far axis: IN crossfaded from the far speaker to the hand-adjacent speaker, while OUT reversed the same approximately 100-cm path over 3000 ms.
trial_sequence: Each 5-s trial had 1 s silence, a 3-s IN or OUT sound, and 1 s silence; tactile targets occurred at one of seven delays (including silent pre/post baselines), while auditory-only catch trials omitted touch; all trials were randomized.
task_response: Participants said 'TAH' as fast as possible to the electrical tactile target and withheld on auditory-only catches; voice onset was captured by relay, but no online response deadline is reported.
jitter_iti_policy: Trials used fixed 1000-ms silence before and after the 3000-ms sound; no random jitter is reported.
soa_schedule: Tactile onset relative to sound onset was -700, 300, 800, 1500, 2200, 2700, and +3600 ms (T0-T6); T1-T5 are bimodal and T0/T6 are silent tactile-only baselines.
tactile_target: A DS7A constant-current stimulator delivered one 100-ms constant-voltage rectangular monophasic electrical pulse through electrodes on the hairy surface of the right index finger, individually set at 60-90 mA after detection/catch calibration.
baseline_trial_contract: Thirty-two tactile-only baselines occurred during silence: T0 (-700 ms from sound onset) and T6 (+3600 ms), eight repetitions for each nominal IN/OUT assignment and endpoint.
catch_trial_contract: Seventy-six auditory-only IN/OUT trials were randomly intermingled; participants withheld the vocal response.
repetition_allocation: Eight tactile-target repetitions at each of seven delays for each of IN and OUT yielded 112 targets (80 critical audio-tactile and 32 tactile-only baseline), plus 76 catches, for 188 total trials.
block_order_contract: The 188 randomized trials were equally split into two blocks of 94, each lasting about 8 minutes.

trial_sequence: Randomized Go/NoGo trials crossed tactile intensity (weak target/strong nontarget) with near/far sound, plus sound-only catch trials; 30 practice trials preceded the task.
task_response: Participants said 'tah' as rapidly as possible only for weak electrical targets, withheld for strong electrical nontargets and sound-only catches, and ignored the sound; no response deadline is reported.
jitter_iti_policy: The publication does not report an intertrial interval or jitter policy.
soa_schedule: Near sound onset was simultaneous with tactile onset; far sound command onset was -5 ms relative to tactile onset to compensate propagation delay.
tactile_target: Weak target and stronger nontarget constant-current electrical stimuli were delivered through two electrode pairs on the right index finger and individually titrated; pulse waveform/duration are not reported.
baseline_trial_contract: The exhaustive five-family, 150-trial inventory contains no tactile-only or other baseline trial family.
catch_trial_contract: Thirty sound-only catch trials were intermingled in every 150-trial condition; no response was expected.
repetition_allocation: Each 150-trial condition contained 30 target-near, 30 target-far, 30 nontarget-near, 30 nontarget-far, and 30 sound-only catch trials.
block_order_contract: Blind participants completed counterbalanced cane and handle 150-trial conditions; sighted participants additionally completed cane measurements immediately after 10-min training and one day later.

task_response: Patients lay reclined with eyes closed, attended to the sounds and vibrations, and were explicitly required to make no overt response.
jitter_iti_policy: Each nominal tactile delay received an additive 0-200 ms jitter in 50-ms steps; the intertrial interval was randomly selected from 1.4, 1.7, and 1.9 s.

tactile_target: A Precision MicroDrives 312-101 shaftless motor delivered 100-ms, 150-Hz vibration to the upper sternum (3 V, 60 mA, 9000 rpm, 5 g, 113 mm2), controlled by a 10-kHz Arduino via ExpyVR.
baseline_trial_contract: Unisensory tactile T trials were the tactile control family: 85 T trials, each containing tactile events at nominal 500, 1500, and 2500 ms plus the same jitter.
catch_trial_contract: The passive protocol had no response-withholding catch family; auditory-only A trials were a unisensory control, not behavioral catches.
repetition_allocation: Exactly 85 trials were presented for each of A, T, and AT (255 trials total); each T/AT trial contained all three tactile timings, and no count exceptions were reported.

auditory_stimulus: A 3250-ms 44.1-kHz burst train was rendered in Max/MSP 6.1.10/Spat with direct sound, early reflections, late reverberation, and LISTEN HRTFs into fixed and looming stereo assets; exact files/project are not supplied.
trajectory_kinematics: The looming source moved at ear level in the frontal-left hemispace (45-degree azimuth) from 640 to 20 cm at 210 cm/s during the 3250-ms asset; the fixed control remained at 640 cm.
trial_sequence: Trials had 300 ms silence, one fixed/looming 3250-ms sound, a left-hand phone vibration at one of six delays or no vibration for catch, then random 1000-1400-ms silence; participants tapped the screen and received visual confirmation.
task_response: Participants tapped the smartphone screen whenever they felt the left-hand vibration, ignored sound, and withheld on auditory-only catches; the analysis retained 100-1000-ms RT, but no online deadline is stated.
jitter_iti_policy: Sound was preceded by fixed 300-ms silence and followed by a randomly distributed 1000-1400-ms silent period.
soa_schedule: Tactile onset minus sound onset was 105, 1625, 2385, 2765, 2955, or 3050 ms, mapping the looming source to 640, 320, 160, 80, 40, or 20 cm; fixed control used the same SOAs at 640 cm.
tactile_target: The Google Pixel 2 XL haptic motor delivered a 50-ms, 155-Hz vibration at maximum amplitude to the phone held in the left hand.
baseline_trial_contract: The fixed-distant audio-tactile condition served as the explicit temporal-expectancy control at the same six SOAs, with 24 repetitions per SOA (144 fixed-control trials); no tactile-only baseline was used.
catch_trial_contract: Auditory-only catches were interspersed; six blocks x 24 catches implies 144 and reconciles 432 total, but the paper prints 184 catches and Fig. 9 says 76 rather than 72 trials per block.
repetition_allocation: Twenty-four repetitions crossed 2 sound movements x 6 delays (288 experimental); total 432 and 6 blocks x (48 experimental +24 catch) imply 144 catches, conflicting with printed 184 and a 76-trial figure caption.
block_order_contract: Six nominal 3-min blocks each contained 48 experimental and 24 catch trials (72), with short breaks and a mandatory 10-min midpoint break; a figure caption instead says 76 and an earlier app description says five practice plus 72 recorded trials per block.

study_label: The Impact of Looming Sound Duration on Peripersonal Space Measurement (a)
title: The Impact of Looming Sound Duration on Peripersonal Space Measurement
auditory_stimulus: A 2-s pink-noise source was synthesized in MATLAB with HRTF cues, propagation delay, and room-temperature air attenuation to move laterally from the participant's right toward the head; the exact noise asset, HRTFs, and referenced code are not supplied in this paper.
trajectory_kinematics: A right-lateral straight trajectory approached the participant's head from 100 cm to 0 cm at 50 cm/s over 2 s.
trial_sequence: One second after fixation appeared, each trial selected 2-second tactile-only baseline, 2-second audio-tactile looming target, or auditory-only catch; touch occurred at one of seven SOAs; participants pressed a button when touch was felt.
task_response: Participants pressed a Cherry MX Blue button with the left hand as soon as the right-palm vibration was felt and withheld on auditory-only catches; no online deadline is reported.
jitter_iti_policy: Trial onset was fixed 1000 ms after fixation-cross appearance; the post-response intertrial interval and any jitter distribution are not reported.
soa_schedule: Tactile onset minus 2-second audio-track onset was 250, 500, 750, 1000, 1250, 1500, 1750 ms, seven equally spaced points that map to the constant-speed trajectory.
tactile_target: An audio-driven haptic actuator under a molded silicone pad at the right palm delivered a 200-ms, 80-Hz sawtooth generated in Audacity on a DAC-synchronized audio channel.
baseline_trial_contract: The tactile-only baseline used the same seven SOAs and 16 repetitions per SOA, yielding 112 baseline trials in the 2-second experiment.
catch_trial_contract: Twenty-one 2-second auditory-only catches were interspersed; no response was expected.
repetition_allocation: Sixteen repetitions crossed two conditions (baseline/audio-tactile) with seven 2-second delays: 224 tactile-target trials (112 per condition), plus 21 catches = 245.
block_order_contract: The 2-second experiment contained one 245-trial PPS block with two scheduled within-block breaks, followed by a questionnaire; experiment order was semi-counterbalanced across participants.
